title: Schedule a meeting for a customer from the list

steps.do: Filter Pipeline = Leads, open a row's ⋯ menu and choose Schedule Meeting.
steps.expect: A modal 'New meeting — <customer name>' opens over the Customers page. You stay on Customers (prod sent you to the pipeline board).
steps.note: modal title 'New meeting — Grant Nakagawa' for row 'Grant Nakagawa'; url stayed /dashboard/customers?pc_pipeline=leads

steps.expect: The modal closes; the table, filters and page are unchanged.

steps.do: Do the same from the Lead Sources 'All customers' table and from one source's pane.
steps.expect: The same 'New meeting — <name>' modal opens in both places.
steps.note: All customers: 'New meeting — Oli Test'; Telemarketing pane: 'New meeting — Janet Shanks'

steps.do: OLIVER ONLY, on a test customer you own: open Schedule Meeting again, pick a type and a date/time, press 'Create meeting'.
steps.expect: Button reads 'Creating…', then the modal closes by itself.

steps.do: Without reloading, look at that customer's row.
steps.expect: Its Pipeline badge moves from Leads to Fresh (with the Leads filter on, the row drops out of the list). The count updates.

steps.do: Open that customer's profile → Meetings tab.

why: e1bb84e7c: Schedule Meeting now opens CreateMeetingModal through openCreateMeeting (modal layer) instead of navigating to the pipeline; a booking calls invalidateMeeting, which now also refreshes the customers list (use-invalidation.ts).
